Certified copy of utility bill or bank statement proving beneficial owner's address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the issuer is not a public authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency and good standing (where beneficial owner is a corporate entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate owner's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each director, shareholder, natural-person beneficial owner, and the anti-money laundering compliance officer against: the UN Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list and US/Sanctions Lists (when transacting in USD/dollars), the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing Unit (EMLCU) domestic list, and PEP databases (World-Check or equivalent). Screening must be refreshed at every client onboarding and annually; adverse hits must be reported to the EMLCU via the dedicated portal within 48 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Tradename/Name Reservation Portal (gafi.gov.eg) and the Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (commercialregistry.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Arabic, or an Arabic transliteration of a foreign name is required. The Arabic name must be registered exactly as set out in the certificate; Latin script is accepted only as a transliteration and must not be misleading. The name must not duplicate any existing name in the Commercial Registry or GAFI's database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term requiring a prior license from the Central Bank of Egypt or the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 days of the rejection notice, providing additional evidence of distinctiveness and a statement of the intended regulated activity. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may request a second level administrative review by GAFI's Arbitration and Recommendation Committee, after which they may initiate judicial review before the Egyptian Administrative Court within 60 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible as the registered office must be a physical address within Egypt that can accept service of process; however a flexible serviced office may be acceptable if a physical desk, reception and compliance files are maintained. For a lending Fintech, the FRA and CBE expect physical operations, so recommendation is a physical office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated > 70% annually) — for a high-risk AML special license (micro lending), the FRA and CBE conduct unannounced periodic inspections, and the EMLCU may also perform on-site AML compliance visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, including Articles 24-58 (limited liability companies) and Articles 92-106 (share capital, quotas, and management); Executive Regulations of Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982; Law No. 22 of 2021 regulating financial technology activities applicable to the micro-lending platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry, Commercial Affairs Administration, Ministry of Trade and Industry; one-stop shop operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of a Limited Liability Company submitted to the GAFI One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed statutory minimum beyond EGP 1,000 under the Companies Law, but the financial regulators may impose a higher paid-up capital condition for peer-to-peer lending activities. The paid-up capital must be deposited in a temporary escrow account at a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt, and the bank confirmation certificate must be submitted to GAFI before issuance of the commercial registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association hereby adopt the following resolutions at the first board meeting: 1. The paid-up share capital subscription of EGP [amount] is accepted and the share register is opened. 2. The registered office shall be established at [address in Egypt], designated as the official seat for service of process and correspondence. 3. The following officers are appointed: Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer, Compliance Officer and Company Secretary, each with authority to execute bank account documentation and regulatory filings. 4. The Company is authorized to apply for all required financial technology licenses and to open escrow and operating accounts with banks authorized by the Central Bank of Egypt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Egypt Business Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the GAFI Egypt Business Platform, search the registered names database, and file the corporate name reservation and non-conflict request for the proposed Arabic and English company name. GAFI verifies availability and issues the name availability certificate after inspecting the preliminary Memorandum of Association.
required_dossiers: Proposed Arabic and English entity names in order of preference
Passport copies of all founding shareholders
Draft Memorandum of Association
Signed authorization letter of the incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is deemed misleading, offensive, or deceptively similar to an existing registration, file a written objection with GAFI's Registration Department within 15 days and simultaneously reserve two alternative names to prevent expiry of the clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Office of the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Arabic Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, incorporating the capital allocation, quota subscriptions, management structure, and statements necessary for the financial technology license. Ensure all shareholders sign before the notary and that the constitutional documents are stamped and notarized.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate
Passports and national identity documents of shareholders
Statement of subscribed capital and percentage quotas
Board structure statement listing the first managers and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the file for substantive correction, amend the Memorandum of Association, re-execute the signatures, and resubmit; no additional fee is charged if the correction is completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and escrow bank confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the LLC, deposit the paid-up share capital, and obtain a bank confirmation letter specifying the amount deposited and the account details to be delivered to GAFI. The funds remain blocked until the company registration is granted.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association
Passports of authorized signatories
First board resolution authorizing the escrow account
Tax identification statement issued for the pre-formation file, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the escrow account on account of KYC or outdated documents, provide a refreshed corporate set or escalate to the bank's internal compliance department; GAFI's banking liaison desk can assist with coordination where delays are systemic.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop incorporation and commercial registry filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop and Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file through the GAFI platform or an authorized service agent. Pay the statutory incorporation fees and commercial registration fees, and obtain the provisional incorporation certificate, commercial registration extract, and forwarding file for tax registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit confirmation certificate
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
Passports and identity cards of shareholders and managers
Name availability certificate
Form 2 incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or substantiation notice, cure the specified omission by submitting corrected declarations within 10 working days; if the filing is rejected, appeal to the GAFI Complaint Committee within 30 days with a written legal brief and any additional consents required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification and tax card registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Central Records Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the automatic transmission of the incorporation record from GAFI to the ETA, apply for a Tax Identification Number (TIN), tax card, VAT registration, stamp duty statement, and electronic-invoice enrollment. Retain the ETA certificate as part of the legal entity's compliance file.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract
Notarized Memorandum of Association
Registered office lease contract
Passports of managers
Bank letter certifying the paid-up capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA assigns an incorrect tax profile or blocks the file, file a rectification request through a certified tax agent within 20 days attaching the MOA and the intended licensing scope; late-registration fines may be abated upon proof that the delay arose from GAFI's processing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance, labor office, and company seal registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) and the Ministry of Manpower Labor Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company establishment file with NOSI, submit the employment contracts of managers and staff, issue the company seal imprint, and record the registered office address for labor inspection purposes. This step completes the statutory formation formalities.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract
Tax card and TIN certificate
Registered office lease contract
Complete list of employees and nomination forms
First board resolution appointing the payroll signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI imposes late-registration penalties, petition with evidence that the application was submitted within the statutory grace period; disputes are adjudicated under Social Insurance Law No. 148 of 2019 before the General Authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) in coordination with the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-Bank Financial Technology License for Peer-to-Peer Micro-Lending and Crowdfunding Platform Activities pursuant to Fintech Law No. 22 of 2021

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (List C) - Registration-only for office-based fintech operations with no industrial process; full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category A or B) is not required unless a data-center footprint, tower infrastructure, or generator sets above regulatory thresholds are introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and Prime Ministerial Decree No. 3388/2013: no process industrial wastewater; sanitary effluent discharged to municipal sewer in accordance with Law No. 93/1962; no VOC or particulate stack emissions; standby generator exhaust limited to applicable ambient air limits; e-waste segregated and transferred only to EEAA-licensed recycling contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate to be obtained from the General Administration of Civil Defense after inspection of emergency exits, alarm systems, and portable extinguishers; structural load and building safety certificate from the competent district municipality; occupational health and safety clearance issued by the Ministry of Manpower for the registered office premises, including workplace ventilation, electrical safety, and staff first-aid requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; electronic services are provided through the ETA Taxpayer Portal and the Egyptian e-Invoice and e-Receipt portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate and register the Egyptian LLC with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones or other competent incorporation authority. 2. Obtain the commercial registration, constitutional documents, registered office evidence, lease or ownership evidence, manager identification, and powers of attorney. 3. Apply to the relevant ETA tax office or through the ETA electronic registration service for a tax registration number and tax card. 4. Register for value added tax if the LLC makes taxable supplies and reaches the statutory turnover threshold, or if voluntary registration is accepted. 5. Submit corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, payroll tax, and other applicable registrations separately where required. 6. Complete ETA portal enrollment, authorized representative verification, and electronic signature setup. 7. Enroll in the e-invoice system before issuing covered B2B invoices and in the e-receipt system where the business falls within the applicable B2C phases. A foreign entity without an Egyptian legal presence generally obtains an Egyptian tax registration only where it has an Egyptian permanent establishment, taxable local activity, VAT registration obligation, withholding or payroll obligation, or another statutory filing nexus. A non-resident supplying electronically supplied services to Egyptian consumers may have separate non-resident VAT compliance obligations where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An Egyptian LLC is generally taxed as a separate legal entity and is subject to Egyptian corporate income tax on its taxable income under the Income Tax Law. Egypt does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for an Egyptian LLC. There is no general election allowing an Egyptian LLC to be treated as a transparent partnership solely by filing a tax form. Tax treatment follows the legal form and applicable statutory rules. Hybrid mismatch elections are not generally available. Special economic-zone, free-zone, investment-law, or sector incentive regimes require separate eligibility and approval and do not constitute a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under the Egyptian Value Added Tax Law and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500000 annual taxable turnover, subject to the statutory rules for compulsory registration, taxable supplies, related persons, and regulated activities. Voluntary registration may be available. Interest and other qualifying financial services may be VAT-exempt, while separately charged technology, platform, underwriting, servicing, brokerage, administration, subscription, or success fees may constitute taxable services and must be analyzed separately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taxpayers within the applicable e-invoicing phases must issue electronic invoices through the ETA e-invoice platform for covered business-to-business and government transactions. The invoice generally requires the supplier and customer tax identifiers, invoice data, taxable value, VAT amount, classification codes, and an ETA-assigned unique identification number. Covered invoices must be digitally signed using an approved electronic signature and submitted through the prescribed API or portal workflow for ETA validation and clearance before use in the applicable cases. The recipient must accept or reject invoices through the system. Businesses covered by the e-receipt phases must issue electronic receipts for covered business-to-consumer transactions through the ETA e-receipt system, normally using approved point-of-sale or API integration. Failure to enroll, issue, transmit, digitally sign, or retain required electronic documents may result in penalties, denial of input VAT credit, suspension of system access, and assessment of unpaid tax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are generally zero-rated where the goods are exported outside Egypt and the export is evidenced by customs records and other prescribed documentation. Services supplied to a non-resident may qualify for zero-rating only where the statutory conditions are satisfied, including non-resident customer status, use or benefit of the service outside Egypt, absence of prohibited Egyptian consumption, and acceptable evidence of payment and export of the service. A platform's lending interest, qualifying financial return, or other exempt financial supply is not converted into a zero-rated export merely because the customer or lender is non-resident. Separately identifiable platform, software, underwriting, servicing, or intermediation fees must be tested independently. Input VAT refunds or credits require valid tax invoices, customs evidence, accounting records, proof of payment where required, and reconciliation to VAT returns. Zero-rating is unavailable where the transaction is actually consumed in Egypt, the customer is not genuinely non-resident, documentation is incomplete, or the supply is VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or electronic customs export record
Commercial invoice and packing list for exported goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport document
Evidence of customs exit and shipment outside Egypt
Foreign-currency bank receipt, inward remittance evidence, or other approved payment evidence for qualifying exported services
Customer contract, purchase order, service agreement, and evidence identifying the non-resident customer
VAT return reconciliation linking the export to the zero-rated turnover
Certificate of origin or other trade document where required by the destination or customs regime
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may deny zero-rating, disallow input VAT recovery, reassess VAT at the applicable domestic rate, and recover the resulting tax, interest, and statutory additional amounts where export evidence, customer status, service-use evidence, customs exit, or payment documentation is deficient. Fraudulent invoices, fictitious exports, concealed taxable supplies, false customs records, or deliberate VAT evasion may trigger administrative penalties, criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment exposure under applicable tax and customs laws, and joint liability for responsible managers or participants. Incorrect VAT returns and failure to issue required invoices may generate separate penalties. Refunds obtained without entitlement may be clawed back with applicable interest and penalties. The 180-day foreign-exchange evidence or repatriation period must be applied only where required by the relevant export, banking, customs, or VAT rules; it is not a universal substitute for transaction-specific statutory documentation. The taxpayer should retain customs, banking, contractual, accounting, and electronic-invoice records for the applicable statutory retention period and be able to produce them during an ETA audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) co-regulates non-bank P2P micro-lending and crowdfunding under Law No. 5 of 2022 amending the Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: EGP operates under a unified managed-float regime following the March 2024 liberalization and the IMF Extended Fund Facility. Current-account transactions (trade, services, royalties, interest) are freely convertible through authorized dealer banks subject to underlying documentation and automatic CBE reporting. Capital-account transactions require prior registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 to secure CBE-guaranteed repatriation rights. Profit remittance for non-resident shareholders is permitted once the Egyptian Tax Authority issues a tax clearance certificate, audited financial statements are filed, dividend withholding tax (10% statutory or reduced treaty rate) is settled, and the settling bank receives a foreign-currency purchase declaration. The practical hurdle is documentation and bank-level FX liquidity, not legal inconvertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory EGP surrender ratio for export proceeds was abolished after the 2024 float. Exporters must route 100% of proceeds through an Egyptian authorized dealer bank within 30 days from customs clearance (extendable to 180 days with CBE approval), retain foreign currency in registered Export Proceeds Accounts, and may convert freely; undocumented parallel holding of proceeds triggers CBE sanctions, account freeze, and loss of trade finance access. For this P2P platform there is no commodity export business; the analogous regime is cross-border financial-inflow declaration: all inbound foreign lender subscriptions and share capital must be routed through the local banking system and registered with CBE to establish the legal basis for later outbound repayments and dividend remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Operational Account and FX Capital Escrow Account
EGP Operational Account, USD Corporate Account and Escrow Account
EGP Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
EGP Operational Account and USD Working Capital Account
USD/EUR Multi-Currency Account and Global Clearing Hub

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-nil as a primary banking layer. Offshore digital EMIs (EU/UK licensed) hold no CBE banking license, cannot access CBE RTGS, the Egypt Instant Payment Network (IPN/InstaPay), or the Egyptian ACH, and cannot lawfully hold EGP client funds. Their only workable role is as a secondary FX conversion and virtual-IBAN aggregation corridor routed to an onshore correspondent bank. A viable arrangement requires contracting with a licensed Egyptian bank under a Banking-as-a-Service platform or entering the CBE Regulatory Sandbox to graduate to a digital bank license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory. Onboarding of a high-risk fintech requires: (i) in-person interview of at least one authorized signatory and every UBO holding 25% or more of the LLC at the bank's corporate branch in Cairo; (ii) originals of corporate documents with Egyptian consular legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; foreign-issued documents must be attested by the Egyptian embassy or consulate in the issuing jurisdiction and then by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs); and (iii) a board resolution authorizing account opening and the CBE beneficiary declaration. Remote e-KYC under CBE's 2020 regulations applies only to low-risk resident individuals and cannot be used for this entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATF increased-monitoring (grey-list) status of Egypt since February 2023, automatically forcing enhanced due diligence on all non-bank fintech and lending platforms regardless of local licensing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed EDD questionnaire; AML/CFT manual aligned with Law No. 80 of 2002 and its executive regulations; Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) appointment filed with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMCLU); enterprise-wide money-laundering and terrorist-financing risk assessment; FATF action-plan remediation evidence; external AML audit opinion issued by an Egyptian-registered audit firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk P2P micro-lending categorization as a special-licensed, non-deposit-taking platform with algorithmic underwriting, creating suspicion of disguised deposit-taking or fund-velocity irregularities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FRA crowdfunding platform license and FRA no-objection letter for the lending algorithm; notarized platform terms and matched lending contracts; segregated escrow account agreement with a CBE-licensed custodian bank; diagram of the funds flow proving matched lender-borrower transactions are segregated from operating assets; FRA regulatory filings for the two most recent quarters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity where a non-resident shareholder controls 100% of the LLC and the 25% UBO disclosure threshold may be bypassed through layered vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration form; certified passport copies of all natural-person shareholders; Commercial Registry extract for the LLC; chain-of-title certificates for every intermediate entity; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations supported by 12-month bank statements, audited financial statements, and income tax filings; external legal opinion confirming the UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and currency-attribution risk on the initial USD/EUR capital injection and subsequent cross-border loan-funding transfers into Egypt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 copies referencing the GAFI investment registration number; latest Egyptian tax clearance certificate; audited balance sheet and certificate of incumbency of the sending entity; FX conversion tickets with dealer confirmation; CBE foreign-investment registration declarations (entry forms) proving lawful inflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hits on the Egyptian director, a UBO, or a borrower wallet flagged in international watchlists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening output with disposition notes; UN, EU, OFAC, and EMCLU list checks; PEP declaration and risk-scoring matrix; client risk reclassification memorandum; de-risking appeal to the CBE Banking Complaints Unit if the account is refused.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder wires funds by SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's FCY or EGP capital account at an authorized dealer bank, referencing the shareholder capital-subscription resolution and GAFI registration number; the bank records the inflow with CBE, converts to EGP at the interbank weighted-average rate where the operating account is EGP-denominated, and requires a stated-purpose declaration (capital subscription, shareholder loan, or crowdfunding participant funds). Inflow above EGP-equivalent 1 million triggers the CBE foreign-investment entry declarations and source-of-wealth documentation; settlement completes same day via the CBE RTGS system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Onshore borrower loans are disbursed through the CBE Egypt Instant Payment Network (IPN/InstaPay) or the Egyptian ACH direct-debit rail to borrower wallets and bank accounts; repayment collections use ACH direct-debit mandates and Meeza domestic cards. Cross-border outflows (dividends, foreign-lender exits, licensing or service fees, refinancing of foreign payables) settle via SWIFT MT103/MT202 through an onshore correspondent bank under a documentary package comprising FRA disbursement approval, FRA platform statements, Egyptian Tax Authority withholding certificate, CBE exit declarations, and the bank's foreign-currency purchase declaration; no commercial letters of credit are required for the pure-lending model.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP and EUR/EGP forward contracts with CBE-authorized dealer banks, conditioned on verified underlying EGP exposure and CBE forward-position limits
Offshore EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through international counterparties for portfolio-level EGP risk hedging
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between EGP and USD/EUR with CBE approval, linked to concrete capital or funding liabilities
Plain-vanilla USD/EGP FX options (call and put) purchased from authorized banks; option writing is not permitted
Natural-hedge netting of lender and borrower positions through a single FX multicurrency pooling account at the settlement bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration Renewal Certificate (Qayd and renewal of the commercial register extract)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, General Department of Commercial Registration, Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days before the anniversary of the original registration date; renewal is required annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs an administrative fine of EGP 500–2,000 (approx. USD 16–65) plus daily delay penalties; failure to renew may lead to suspension of the commercial license and administrative strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (UBO Register confirmation) covering share transfers and ultimate natural persons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Beneficial Ownership Registry Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March each year following the end of the calendar year; updates required within 15 days of any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or misdeclaration triggers a warning, then a fine from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 (approx. USD 650–3,300); continuous default can lead to suspension of the company's file with GAFI and initiation of administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent audited annual financial statements (EAS-compliant) together with the directors' report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and GAFI; copies retained in the company's statutory register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year end; the fiscal year is state 31 December unless a different period is approved by the ETA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission exposes the company to a fine of EGP 5,000–20,000 (approx. USD 165–650) under Investment Law; for the licensed P2P lending entity, the Central Bank of Egypt may impose additional license-level penalties and restrict future renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 221) with audited financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority, Large Taxpayer Center (LTC) if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the end of the fiscal year for a clear 31 December year end; for approved special fiscal years, 4 months from that year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties equal 2% of the tax due per month (capped at 120% of the tax); non-filing invokes additional fixed fines of EGP 10,000 (approx. USD 330) plus administrative seizure actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card Renewal Application (renewal of the active tax card for the licensed lending activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority – Tax Card Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before 31 December of the expiring year; valid for one calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal causes the tax card to lapse, disabling bank account operations and customs transactions; late renewal incurs a fine of EGP 1,000 (approx. USD 33) and interest on any undecided tax obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to all licensed P2P micro-lending entities irrespective of size due to the Central Bank of Egypt's financial technology license requirements; additionally, under Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, any LLC with capital exceeding EGP 250,000 or more than 10 shareholders must appoint a certified external auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as issued by the Ministry of Finance and the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority; EAS are aligned with IFRS for business entities, and the National Court of Accounts requires full EAS-compliant statements for licensed lending companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: After every annual general meeting and before the statutory annual declaration of 31 March, the LLC must review and confirm the register of beneficial owners, verifying that any share transfers, pledges, or changes in indirect control are reflected. The UBO register must be kept at the registered office and submitted to GAFI through its online system; failing to confirm annually triggers administrative penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–800 per year for office rental insurance and registered agent services in Cairo or Alexandria
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–6,000 per year, depending on transaction volume, fintech compliance testing, and the independent audit firm's complexity adjustments for ISIC 6499 micro-lending operations
